newsitem.title: UK: Bradys lack fresh impetus, Bulgaria shaves gains.
newsitem.headline: Bradys lack fresh impetus, Bulgaria shaves gains.

text.p: A lacklustre Brady bond market saw little trade on Tuesday morning amid nervousness about future U.S. interest rate rises and a lack of fresh impetus, dealers said.

"The market is still expecting U.S. Treasuries to weaken as a result of rising U.S. interest rates which is having a dampening effect on (Brady bond) volumes and the market is listless," an analyst said.
"Its a low volatility quiet day. There's a whole spate of (U.S.) data due next week, there's bad news ahead and so its difficult to buy into these conditions," he added.
Bulgaria gained ground on Monday following the weekend election victory of the "market-friendly" Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), but profit-taking on Tuesday saw prices down.
Bulgaria's benchmark IAB was at 60 bid at 1030 GMT versus 61-1/8 bid around the same time on Monday.
Bulgaria's FLRB bid at 44-5/8 versus 45-3/4 bid on Monday.
Bulgaria's DISCs were bid at 62 versus 62-5/8 bid on Monday.
"The market had already discounted Bulgaria's news," a dealer said. "There's not as much interest in Bulgaria this morning," he added.
But some still reckoned Bulgarian Bradys were "cheap" and offered value.
Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) said Bulgarian Bradys could outperform the global Brady index.
It forecast Bulgaria's benchmark IAB rising to 63 in July, 65 in September and 67 by December this year.
FLRBs were expected to climb to 51 by December and DISCs to 69 by year-end.
